subject: Copywriting
title: Just Do It: Three Words, Billions
description: A fast breakdown of Just Do It: Three Words, Billions for builders.

hook.text: In 1988, Nike was losing to Reebok. Dan Wieden wrote three words that turned it around: 'Just Do It.'

buildup.text: Wieden said the phrase was inspired by a death row inmate's last words: 'Let's do it.' He changed 'let's' to 'just.'

discovery.text: The line worked because it wasn't about shoes. It was about overcoming hesitation. Universal and timeless.

twist.text: Nike's sales went from $877M to $9.2B in ten years. Three words generated more value than any product feature.

climax.text: Every great tagline transcends its product. 'Just Do It' could sell anything. That's the mark of perfect copy.

punchline.text: Three words. $877M to $9.2B. That's a tagline.

quiz.question: What was Nike's revenue before 'Just Do It'?

details.summary: Nike's 'Just Do It' is perhaps the most successful three-word headline in commercial history. What began as a campaign tagline became a global motivational mantra. It demonstrates that the best advertising headlines transcend products entirely, speaking directly to human aspiration.
details.whyItMatters: Just Do It proves that a headline can define not just a product but an attitude toward life. Understanding how three words generated billions in value reveals the power of emotional simplicity.
takeaways: Three words drove Nike from $877M to $9.2B in revenue within a decade
The headline works because it addresses human hesitation universally
It transcended advertising to become a cultural motivational phrase

faq.question: Why does 'Just Do It' work as a headline?
faq.answer: It bypasses product features entirely and addresses the universal human experience of hesitation. Everyone has something they've been putting off. Three monosyllabic words delivered as a command create an irresistible call to action that applies to running, working, and living.

faq.question: Can modern brands create headlines as impactful as 'Just Do It'?
faq.answer: It's extremely rare but not impossible. The conditions require a perfect alignment of cultural moment, brand positioning, and creative execution. Most 'Just Do It' moments are recognized only in retrospect. The lesson is to aim for emotional universality, not product specificity.
